figures.name: Text in, text out
figures.one_idea: The model turns text into one more token, appends it, and does it again.
figures.caption: FIGURE 4.1 — Pick, append, repeat.
figures.accent: the new token and the append path

figures.name: What the model sees
figures.one_idea: The model keeps nothing between calls; the whole window is re-sent every time.
figures.caption: FIGURE 2 — The model reads all of it, every call, and keeps none of it.
figures.accent: the bracket spanning every bar, and the single arrow it feeds

figures.name: Model, your code, tools
figures.one_idea: The model never runs a tool. It asks, and your code runs it.
figures.caption: FIGURE 3 — The model asks. Your code is what actually runs.
figures.accent: the tool-call arrow, at the point it crosses into your code

figures.name: The agent loop
figures.one_idea: An agent is that round trip repeated until the model stops asking.
figures.caption: FIGURE 4 — The loop, and the one way out of it.
figures.accent: the exit arrow and its reply label — the stop condition

figures.name: Where memory lives
figures.one_idea: Memory is a place outside the window that you read in before the call and write back after.
figures.caption: FIGURE 4.3.1 — Memory that survives the window: a file.
figures.accent: the arrow up from memory and the bars it becomes inside the window

figures.name: Gates around the loop
figures.one_idea: Guardrails are checks your code owns on the wires in, out, and to the tools.
figures.caption: FIGURE 6 — Three gates your code owns, around a loop it doesn't.
figures.accent: the three check diamonds

figures.name: Many loops — the Desk
figures.one_idea: A system is several copies of the same loop, each with its own window, wired in a line.
figures.caption: FIGURE 7 — The Desk. Every part is a loop you have already built.
figures.accent: the three research loops running at once

figures.name: A ranked list
figures.one_idea: The output is a whole ranked distribution, and even the winning token is a sliver of it.
figures.caption: FIGURE 3.1 — Not an answer. A list of possible next tokens, with odds.
figures.accent: the top bar, filled solid

figures.name: Ninety percent, ten times
figures.one_idea: Per-step reliability multiplies: 90% a step leaves a third of the task standing by step ten.
figures.caption: FIGURE 5.5.1 — Small per-step errors, large end-to-end failure.
figures.accent: the 90% survivor bar, filled solid

figures.name: One run, read back
figures.one_idea: Nesting shows who called whom, a shared time axis shows what ran at once, one bar shows where the time went.
figures.caption: FIGURE 8.6.1 — One run, fully visible. This is the page people will stare at.
figures.accent: the straggler span, filled solid

figures.name: The lethal trifecta
figures.one_idea: No single capability is dangerous; the breach is one agent holding private data, untrusted text, and a way out at the same time.
figures.caption: FIGURE 6.4.1 — Any two is a risk. All three is a breach waiting to happen.
figures.accent: the send tool and the one continuous path through the model

figures.name: Nearest in meaning
figures.one_idea: Chunks sit in a space of meaning, and only the few nearest the question ever enter the window.
figures.caption: FIGURE 4.4.1 — Don't load the library; load the three pages that matter.
figures.accent: the three nearest chunks and the bars they become

figures.name: Folding the transcript
figures.one_idea: Compaction folds the old turns into one summary block, leaves the recent turns verbatim, and gives the window room again.
figures.caption: FIGURE 4.2.1 — Compaction: trade detail for room.
figures.accent: the one dense summary block

figures.name: The round trip, in order
figures.one_idea: A tool result is just another message in the window — the model reads it, it does not know it.
figures.caption: FIGURE 3.3.1 — One tool use is two messages and a function call in between.
figures.accent: the tool-result bar

figures.name: What sits inside what
figures.one_idea: A language model is one specific thing inside a much larger field, and it is the only part this course starts from.
figures.caption: FIGURE 0.1 — Four words people use interchangeably, drawn to scale.
figures.accent: the language model, the innermost ring

figures.name: The four layers
figures.one_idea: You do not build the model or the hardware; you build the orchestration layer between the model and the application.
figures.caption: FIGURE 0.2 — Four layers. You work in one of them.
figures.accent: the orchestration layer

figures.name: Workflow or agent
figures.one_idea: In a workflow you decide the path in advance; in an agent the model decides it at run time.
figures.caption: FIGURE 7.1.1 — Who chooses the next step: you, or the model.
figures.accent: the model's choice, and the branch it took

figures.name: Five shapes
figures.one_idea: Every multi-agent system is one of five wiring patterns, and the one you build is a lead with workers.
figures.caption: FIGURE 7.2.1 — Five ways to wire loops together.
figures.accent: the three workers running under a lead

figures.name: Who is working when
figures.one_idea: Fanning out is a claim about time: two researchers occupy the same stretch of the clock.
figures.caption: FIGURE 7.3.1 — The same work, laid out on the clock.
figures.accent: the two research lanes that overlap

figures.name: The harness
figures.one_idea: The loop stays the loop; what turns it into a system is four services hanging off it.
figures.caption: FIGURE 8.4.1 — One loop, four services. The harness is everything below the line.
figures.accent: the loop the harness is built around
